title: Maryland resends thousands of mail-in primary ballots after vendor mix-up
summary: Thousands of Maryland voters will be getting new primary election ballots in the mail after the State Board of Elections announced Friday that some voters received the wrong party’s ballot for the June 23 primary because of a vendor error.
content:
By Tracy Johnke

Thousands of Maryland voters will be getting new primary election ballots in the mail after an error was discovered in the first batch.

The State Board of Elections announced Friday that some voters received the wrong party’s ballot for the June 23 primary because of a vendor error.

“It is possible only a small number of voters received the wrong ballot, and most voters received the correct ballot,” the board said in its statement on the mix-up.

Even though only a small number of voters are believed to have been involved, the statement went on to say that all voters who received a mail-in ballot so far must be sent a replacement, which “maintains the integrity and security of mail-in voting.”

“Mail-in voting is an integral facet of the electoral process. With over 500,000 voters requesting mail-in ballots, we want to eliminate any doubt in its integrity or accuracy … that is why I have arranged the sending of replacement ballots,” Maryland State Administrator of Elections Jared DeMarinis said.

In a statement from the printer provided by the board, Taylor Print and Visual Impressions Inc. said it has “implemented additional quality control and verification measures to help prevent this type of issue from occurring in the future.”

The affected ballots were requested and mailed before May 14, more than a month before the state’s June 16 deadline for voters who wish to have their ballots mailed to them.

Voters who requested ballots that can be downloaded, printed and mailed were not affected by the error. They have until June 22 — the day before the state’s primary election — to request ballots by web delivery.

The Maryland Freedom Caucus, a group of seven hard-right House conservatives, seized on the error and said the state should not resend ballots to correct it.

“We demand to know how the state intends to differentiate between the first and second printing of these ballots,” the caucus said in a statement on the issue Saturday. “The citizens have a right to know the exact process by which ballots will be scrutinized.”

In a frequently asked questions portion of its statement, the printer said there is “no risk of duplicate voting as a result of this issue. Election officials have safeguards in place to ensure that only the corrected ballots included in the replacement mailing will be accepted and counted,” it said, without specifying those safeguards.

DeMarinis said his office is “diligently working to address this error and provide clear instructions to those affected

as quickly as possible.”

“Please be assured that we are actively answering phones and responding to emails and will remain transparent as we navigate through this situation,” DeMarinis said. “We will make every effort to ensure that everyone affected knows the situation and how to cast their ballot.”
author: WTOP News
